CHAPTER XIII

CRIMINAL SANCTIONS

Article 63

Every person or institution that commits acts resulting in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, coercion, or deprivation of freedom against women and children so that violations of this regional regulation occur, shall be subject to criminal sanctions in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: Region is Tanah Toraja Regency. Regent is the Regent of Tana Toraja. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the regional government and the regional house of representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution that is positioned as an element of the Regional Government administrator. Sub-district is a part of the regency area that is led by a sub-district head. Lembang is another term for village which is part of the regency area that is led by the Head of Lembang; Lembang Government is the term for village government in Tana Toraja Regency. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and children or mother and children or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward laterally to the third degree. Parents are biological father and/or mother or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises custody power as a parent over a child. Woman is a human being who can menstruate, become pregnant, give birth and breastfeed. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a baby still in the womb. Neglected Child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. Protection of women is all efforts made to ensure the fulfillment of women's rights as a form of respect for human rights. Women's empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social capacity, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has special potential and/or talent not limited to intellectual ability, but also in other fields. Adopted Child is a Child whose rights are transferred from the environment of the authority of the Family of Parents, legal Guardian, or other person responsible for the care, education, and raising of the Child into the environment of the adoptive Parents' Family based on a court decision or determination. Foster Child is a Child who is cared for by a person or institution to be provided with guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health because the Parents or one of the Parents is unable to guarantee the proper growth and development of the Child. Custody is the power of Parents to care for, educate, maintain, foster, protect, and develop the Child in accordance with the religion professed and in accordance with the Child's abilities, talents, and interests. Child's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. Companion is a social worker who has professional competence in their field. Violence is any act unlawfully, which results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and mistreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a cooperative network that carries out integrated social service functions. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is a cooperative network that carries out integrated service functions for the protection of women and children. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and/or other community organizations. Family Welfare Consultation Institution hereinafter abbreviated as LK3 is an integrated social service unit that implements family psychosocial problem handling to realize family resilience. Regional Child Protection Commission hereinafter abbreviated as KPAD is an integrated social service unit that implements child protection services to realize the fulfillment of children's rights.

ELUCIDATION

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANA TORAJA REGENCY

NUMBER 4 YEAR 2017

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

GENERAL

Women and children are God's creatures who have dignity and human rights that need to be respected and valued.

Women are the pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the nation's next generation, need to get the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.

Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity of women and children, they are vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.

Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to give serious attention and handling, it will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state.

Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is able to answer while providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.

As a concrete step in an effort to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 of 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 of 2015 concerning the System of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation is intended to give responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing acts of violence to handling victims of violence.

In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of regional government, responsibilities of Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.

This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other non-binding sources, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

Article 50

The obligations and responsibilities of parents and family as referred to in Article 45 letter d, are to safeguard and prevent the occurrence of all forms of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination both against women and against children.

The obligations and responsibilities of parents towards children as referred to in paragraph (1), are to: care for, maintain, educate, and protect children;

develop children according to their abilities, talents, and interests;

prevent marriage at child age; and provide character education and instillation of moral values in children.

Guardians and/or foster parents who have obtained a determination as referred to in Article 46 paragraph (3), must be able to fulfill the provisions as referred to in article 36 paragraph (2) letter a.

Guardians and/or foster parents appointed as referred to in paragraph (3) must have the same religion as that professed by the Child.

Guardians and/or foster parents as referred to in paragraph (3) are responsible for the child and are obliged to manage the property of the child concerned for the best interests of the child.

Guardians and/or foster parents as referred to in paragraph (3), may represent the child to perform legal acts, both inside and outside the court for the best interests of the child.

Article 41

The Regional Government provides special protection for children exploited economically and/or sexually as referred to in Article 37 letter d and child victims of violence both physical and mental as referred to in Article 37 letter h.

Special protection for exploited children and child victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through: socialization of laws and regulations related to the protection of children exploited economically and/or sexually;

monitoring, reporting, and imposition of sanctions; and involvement of various organizations, Regional Government, companies, labor unions, social institutions and the community.

Article 47

In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in Article 46 paragraph (1), the Regent establishes programs and activities for the protection of women and children in the regional action plan as a basis for regional apparatus in implementing the protection of women and children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

The regional action plan as referred to in paragraph (1), is part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMD).

Further provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (2) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Part Four

Protection of Women

Article 34

Protection in the field of education as referred to in Article 30 paragraph (1), applies both outside the school environment and within the school environment.

Protection outside the school environment is to protect and prevent children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

Protection in the school environment is protection from acts of violence that can be committed either by school administrators, by teachers, or by their own friends.

Paragraph 1

Prevention of Violence

Article 21

Every child who becomes a perpetrator or victim of sexual violence or who is in conflict with the law has the right to confidentiality.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANA TORAJA REGENCY

NUMBER 4 YEAR 2017

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

GENERAL

Women and children are God's creatures who have dignity and human rights that need to be respected and valued.

Women are the pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the nation's next generation, need to get the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.

Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity of women and children, they are vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.

Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to give serious attention and handling, it will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state.

Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is able to answer while providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.

As a concrete step in an effort to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 of 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 of 2015 concerning the System of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation is intended to give responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing acts of violence to handling victims of violence.

In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of regional government, responsibilities of Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.

This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other non-binding sources, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

Article 47

In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in Article 46 paragraph (1), the Regent establishes programs and activities for the protection of women and children in the regional action plan as a basis for regional apparatus in implementing the protection of women and children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

The regional action plan as referred to in paragraph (1), is part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMD).

Further provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (2) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

NUMBER 4 YEAR 2017

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

GENERAL

Women and children are God's creatures who have dignity and human rights that need to be respected and valued.

Women are the pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the nation's next generation, need to get the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.

Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity of women and children, they are vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.

Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to give serious attention and handling, it will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state.

Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is able to answer while providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.

As a concrete step in an effort to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 of 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 of 2015 concerning the System of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation is intended to give responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing acts of violence to handling victims of violence.

In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of regional government, responsibilities of Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.

This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other non-binding sources, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

monitoring, reporting, and imposition of sanctions; and involvement of various organizations, Regional Government, companies, labor unions, social institutions and the community.

NUMBER 4 YEAR 2017

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

GENERAL

Women and children are God's creatures who have dignity and human rights that need to be respected and valued.

Women are the pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the nation's next generation, need to get the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.

Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity of women and children, they are vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.

Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to give serious attention and handling, it will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state.

Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is able to answer while providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.

As a concrete step in an effort to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 of 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 of 2015 concerning the System of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation is intended to give responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing acts of violence to handling victims of violence.

In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of regional government, responsibilities of Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.

This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other non-binding sources, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

develop children according to their abilities, talents, and interests;

prevent marriage at child age; and provide character education and instillation of moral values in children.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANA TORAJA REGENCY

NUMBER 4 YEAR 2017

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

GENERAL

Women and children are God's creatures who have dignity and human rights that need to be respected and valued.

Women are the pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the nation's next generation, need to get the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.

Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity of women and children, they are vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.

Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to give serious attention and handling, it will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state.

Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is able to answer while providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.

As a concrete step in an effort to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 of 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 of 2015 concerning the System of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation is intended to give responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing acts of violence to handling victims of violence.

In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of regional government, responsibilities of Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.

This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other non-binding sources, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

NUMBER 4 YEAR 2017

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

GENERAL

Women and children are God's creatures who have dignity and human rights that need to be respected and valued.

Women are the pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the nation's next generation, need to get the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.

Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity of women and children, they are vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.

Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to give serious attention and handling, it will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state.

Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is able to answer while providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.

As a concrete step in an effort to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 of 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 of 2015 concerning the System of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation is intended to give responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing acts of violence to handling victims of violence.

In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of regional government, responsibilities of Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.

This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other non-binding sources, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

GENERAL

Women and children are God's creatures who have dignity and human rights that need to be respected and valued.

Women are the pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the nation's next generation, need to get the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.

Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity of women and children, they are vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.

Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to give serious attention and handling, it will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state.

Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is able to answer while providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.

As a concrete step in an effort to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 of 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 of 2015 concerning the System of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation is intended to give responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing acts of violence to handling victims of violence.

In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of regional government, responsibilities of Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.

This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other non-binding sources, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

Women and children are God's creatures who have dignity and human rights that need to be respected and valued.

Women are the pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the nation's next generation, need to get the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.

Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity of women and children, they are vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.

Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to give serious attention and handling, it will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state.

Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is able to answer while providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.

As a concrete step in an effort to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 of 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 of 2015 concerning the System of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation is intended to give responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing acts of violence to handling victims of violence.

In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of regional government, responsibilities of Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.

This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other non-binding sources, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANA TORAJA REGENCY

NUMBER 4 YEAR 2017

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

GENERAL

Women and children are God's creatures who have dignity and human rights that need to be respected and valued.

Women are the pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the nation's next generation, need to get the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.

Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity of women and children, they are vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.

Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to give serious attention and handling, it will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state.

Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is able to answer while providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.

As a concrete step in an effort to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 of 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 of 2015 concerning the System of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation is intended to give responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing acts of violence to handling victims of violence.

In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of regional government, responsibilities of Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.

This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other non-binding sources, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

NUMBER 4 YEAR 2017

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

GENERAL

Women and children are God's creatures who have dignity and human rights that need to be respected and valued.

Women are the pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the nation's next generation, need to get the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.

Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity of women and children, they are vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.

Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to give serious attention and handling, it will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state.

Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is able to answer while providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.

As a concrete step in an effort to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 of 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 of 2015 concerning the System of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation is intended to give responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing acts of violence to handling victims of violence.

In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of regional government, responsibilities of Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.

This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other non-binding sources, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANA TORAJA REGENCY

NUMBER 4 YEAR 2017

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

GENERAL

Women and children are God's creatures who have dignity and human rights that need to be respected and valued.

Women are the pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the nation's next generation, need to get the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.

Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity of women and children, they are vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.

Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to give serious attention and handling, it will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state.

Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is able to answer while providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.

As a concrete step in an effort to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 of 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 of 2015 concerning the System of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation is intended to give responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing acts of violence to handling victims of violence.

In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of regional government, responsibilities of Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.

This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other non-binding sources, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

Article 41

The Regional Government provides special protection for children exploited economically and/or sexually as referred to in Article 37 letter d and child victims of violence both physical and mental as referred to in Article 37 letter h.

Special protection for exploited children and child victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through: socialization of laws and regulations related to the protection of children exploited economically and/or sexually;

monitoring, reporting, and imposition of sanctions; and involvement of various organizations, Regional Government, companies, labor unions, social institutions and the community.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

GENERAL

Women and children are God's creatures who have dignity and human rights that need to be respected and valued.

Women are the pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the nation's next generation, need to get the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.

Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity of women and children, they are vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.

Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to give serious attention and handling, it will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state.

Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is able to answer while providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.

As a concrete step in an effort to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 of 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 of 2015 concerning the System of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation is intended to give responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing acts of violence to handling victims of violence.

In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of regional government, responsibilities of Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.

This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other non-binding sources, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity of women and children, they are vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.

Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to give serious attention and handling, it will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state.

Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is able to answer while providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.

As a concrete step in an effort to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 of 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 of 2015 concerning the System of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation is intended to give responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing acts of violence to handling victims of violence.

In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of regional government, responsibilities of Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.

This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other non-binding sources, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: Region is Tanah Toraja Regency. Regent is the Regent of Tana Toraja. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the regional government and the regional house of representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution that is positioned as an element of the Regional Government administrator. Sub-district is a part of the regency area that is led by a sub-district head. Lembang is another term for village which is part of the regency area that is led by the Head of Lembang; Lembang Government is the term for village government in Tana Toraja Regency. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and children or mother and children or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward laterally to the third degree. Parents are biological father and/or mother or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises custody power as a parent over a child. Woman is a human being who can menstruate, become pregnant, give birth and breastfeed. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a baby still in the womb. Neglected Child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. Protection of women is all efforts made to ensure the fulfillment of women's rights as a form of respect for human rights. Women's empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social capacity, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has special potential and/or talent not limited to intellectual ability, but also in other fields. Adopted Child is a Child whose rights are transferred from the environment of the authority of the Family of Parents, legal Guardian, or other person responsible for the care, education, and raising of the Child into the environment of the adoptive Parents' Family based on a court decision or determination. Foster Child is a Child who is cared for by a person or institution to be provided with guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health because the Parents or one of the Parents is unable to guarantee the proper growth and development of the Child. Custody is the power of Parents to care for, educate, maintain, foster, protect, and develop the Child in accordance with the religion professed and in accordance with the Child's abilities, talents, and interests. Child's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. Companion is a social worker who has professional competence in their field. Violence is any act unlawfully, which results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and mistreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a cooperative network that carries out integrated social service functions. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is a cooperative network that carries out integrated service functions for the protection of women and children. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and/or other community organizations. Family Welfare Consultation Institution hereinafter abbreviated as LK3 is an integrated social service unit that implements family psychosocial problem handling to realize family resilience. Regional Child Protection Commission hereinafter abbreviated as KPAD is an integrated social service unit that implements child protection services to realize the fulfillment of children's rights.

Article 47

In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in Article 46 paragraph (1), the Regent establishes programs and activities for the protection of women and children in the regional action plan as a basis for regional apparatus in implementing the protection of women and children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

The regional action plan as referred to in paragraph (1), is part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMD).

Further provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (2) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 50

The obligations and responsibilities of parents and family as referred to in Article 45 letter d, are to safeguard and prevent the occurrence of all forms of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination both against women and against children.

The obligations and responsibilities of parents towards children as referred to in paragraph (1), are to: care for, maintain, educate, and protect children;

develop children according to their abilities, talents, and interests;

prevent marriage at child age; and provide character education and instillation of moral values in children.

Guardians and/or foster parents who have obtained a determination as referred to in Article 46 paragraph (3), must be able to fulfill the provisions as referred to in article 36 paragraph (2) letter a.

Guardians and/or foster parents appointed as referred to in paragraph (3) must have the same religion as that professed by the Child.

Guardians and/or foster parents as referred to in paragraph (3) are responsible for the child and are obliged to manage the property of the child concerned for the best interests of the child.

Guardians and/or foster parents as referred to in paragraph (3), may represent the child to perform legal acts, both inside and outside the court for the best interests of the child.

Article 36

NUMBER 4 YEAR 2017

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

GENERAL

Women and children are God's creatures who have dignity and human rights that need to be respected and valued.

Women are the pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the nation's next generation, need to get the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.

Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity of women and children, they are vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.

Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to give serious attention and handling, it will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state.

Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is able to answer while providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.

As a concrete step in an effort to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 of 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 of 2015 concerning the System of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation is intended to give responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing acts of violence to handling victims of violence.

In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of regional government, responsibilities of Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.

This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other non-binding sources, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: Region is Tanah Toraja Regency. Regent is the Regent of Tana Toraja. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the regional government and the regional house of representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution that is positioned as an element of the Regional Government administrator. Sub-district is a part of the regency area that is led by a sub-district head. Lembang is another term for village which is part of the regency area that is led by the Head of Lembang; Lembang Government is the term for village government in Tana Toraja Regency. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and children or mother and children or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward laterally to the third degree. Parents are biological father and/or mother or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises custody power as a parent over a child. Woman is a human being who can menstruate, become pregnant, give birth and breastfeed. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a baby still in the womb. Neglected Child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. Protection of women is all efforts made to ensure the fulfillment of women's rights as a form of respect for human rights. Women's empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social capacity, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has special potential and/or talent not limited to intellectual ability, but also in other fields. Adopted Child is a Child whose rights are transferred from the environment of the authority of the Family of Parents, legal Guardian, or other person responsible for the care, education, and raising of the Child into the environment of the adoptive Parents' Family based on a court decision or determination. Foster Child is a Child who is cared for by a person or institution to be provided with guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health because the Parents or one of the Parents is unable to guarantee the proper growth and development of the Child. Custody is the power of Parents to care for, educate, maintain, foster, protect, and develop the Child in accordance with the religion professed and in accordance with the Child's abilities, talents, and interests. Child's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. Companion is a social worker who has professional competence in their field. Violence is any act unlawfully, which results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and mistreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a cooperative network that carries out integrated social service functions. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is a cooperative network that carries out integrated service functions for the protection of women and children. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and/or other community organizations. Family Welfare Consultation Institution hereinafter abbreviated as LK3 is an integrated social service unit that implements family psychosocial problem handling to realize family resilience. Regional Child Protection Commission hereinafter abbreviated as KPAD is an integrated social service unit that implements child protection services to realize the fulfillment of children's rights.

Gender mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of national development program policies. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life. Article 27

Parents and families provide protection to maintain the health of children starting from examination of the child's growth and development from the womb.

In the event that parents and families are unable to carry out the protection as referred to in paragraph (1), then the Regional Government is obliged to fulfill it.

The Regional Government provides free assistance and services for underprivileged communities as referred to in paragraph (2), and its implementation is carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 26

Protection in the field of health as referred to in Article 25 paragraph (2) letter a, is carried out by the government through the provision of health facilities and efforts to provide comprehensive health services for children, so that every child obtains the optimal degree of health from the womb.

Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative efforts, both for basic health services and referrals.

Comprehensive health service efforts as referred to in paragraph (2) are implemented by the Regional Government free of charge for families who are unable to afford it.

Article 47

In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in Article 46 paragraph (1), the Regent establishes programs and activities for the protection of women and children in the regional action plan as a basis for regional apparatus in implementing the protection of women and children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

The regional action plan as referred to in paragraph (1), is part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMD).

Further provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (2) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Part Three

Lembang Government

Article 30

Every child receives protection in the field of education as referred to in Article 25 paragraph (2) letter c, to obtain education.

The Regional Government, parents, and families must provide the widest possible opportunity for children to obtain education from an early age.

The Regional Government provides adequate facilities and infrastructure to support the teaching and learning process for children.

Non-governmental institutions may provide teaching and learning facilities and infrastructure for children, in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 36

Child protection in the Social field as referred to in Article 25 paragraph (2) letter d, includes maintenance and care of neglected children.

Maintenance and care as referred to in paragraph (1), includes: fulfillment of basic needs consisting of clothing, food, shelter, education, health, security guarantees, freedom to worship according to their religion and equal treatment with other children to achieve optimal social integration; and fulfillment of special needs for children with disabilities.

Maintenance of neglected children as referred to in paragraph (1), can also be carried out by individuals and non-governmental institutions or community institutions.

Government institutions, and/or individuals, and/or community institutions in providing services as referred to in paragraph (2), may cooperate with various related service units.

Supervision of the implementation of maintenance and care as referred to in paragraph (1), is carried out by regional apparatus organizations (OPD) that administer affairs in the social field in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 41

The Regional Government provides special protection for children exploited economically and/or sexually as referred to in Article 37 letter d and child victims of violence both physical and mental as referred to in Article 37 letter h.

Special protection for exploited children and child victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through: socialization of laws and regulations related to the protection of children exploited economically and/or sexually;

monitoring, reporting, and imposition of sanctions; and involvement of various organizations, Regional Government, companies, labor unions, social institutions and the community.

Part Four

Community

Article 13

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility in efforts to empower women.

The efforts to empower women as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
